agree.reason: The all-or-nothing promise and the frank account of the failed first campaign would probably get this reader to pledge something, but nothing here makes the case for a larger gift from someone who just gave $200 to the ambulance fund.

honest.reason: The numbers are accurate, but 'Your money only goes into the project if we can finish it' ignores a roof estimate that could rise by up to 15%, 'Many of you gave then' is assumed, and the 'This time is different' list includes $1 rent and volunteers without showing either is new.

works_the_facts.reason: The 76-mile round trip and 'nearly a third' are good derivations, but the draft leaves out the $11,000 already pledged in writing, which would cut the public's ask to $49,000, and it never turns 180 tickets a week or the $49,000 into a per-household or per-week figure.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative accurately: no cinema in town and a 38-mile drive to the nearest one, plus steady attendance before closing, without adding a trend the facts don't support.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing condition gives a date (June 30), a figure ($85,000) and a consequence (every pledge returned in full), but the draft says nothing about the roof cost possibly rising 15% or the Thanksgiving reopening target.

objections.reason: It deals with the refund history head-on, but it leaves out the quarterly spending reports and the $11,000 in written pledges that would answer this reader's trust and 'will it work this time' doubts, and it ignores the pull of competing local causes.

fit.reason: It is a clear, well-structured crowdfunding pitch, under 350 words, signed by the chair.
